text: Chronic unpredictable stress altered anxiety-like responses to the cannabinoid CB(1) receptor agonist HU-210 [3-(1,1-dimethylheptyl)-(-)-11-hydroxy-delta 8-tetrahydrocannabinol] in the elevated plus maze. Male Long-Evans rats were either unstressed or exposed to a 21-day chronic unpredictable stress regimen, then assigned to vehicle, 10, or 50 microg/kg HU-210 groups. In unstressed animals, the low dose produced an anxiolytic response while the high dose produced an anxiogenic response. In stressed animals, both the low and high doses induced anxiogenic responses. These findings suggest that chronic stress enhances cannabinoid receptor responsivity, or the responsivity of interacting systems implicated in emotional states.
